summary.text: A 43-year-old male smoker with no prior medical history or current medication presented to a local hospital with severe central chest pain after three days of intermittent chest discomfort and pyrexia. He received aspirin and clopidogrel loading doses and was transferred emergently to a tertiary cardiac centre, where he was haemodynamically stable but hypoxic and cyanosed, with ST-segment changes on ECG and a bedside echocardiogram consistent with an extensive left anterior descending artery territory myocardial infarction.

Coronary angiography showed an occluded dominant right coronary artery, a proximal left anterior descending occlusion with thrombus and a severe left circumflex lesion. After heparin the left anterior descending artery was stented; the patient then developed ventricular tachycardia progressing to pulseless electrical activity cardiac arrest, was resuscitated with automated chest compressions and intubation, and was placed on peripheral veno-arterial ECMO. The right coronary and circumflex lesions were then stented with TIMI 3 flow restored.

Left ventricular function did not improve despite revascularization and inotropes, a repeat echocardiogram showed severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction below 5%, and an Impella 5.0 was inserted on Day 3; the peripheral ECMO cannulae were later removed. Initial swabs and the first lavage were negative for SARS-CoV-2, but a second lavage sample on Day 6 was positive. With progressive deterioration in gas exchange he was proned for 24 hours on Day 8, which improved gas exchange, and a tracheostomy was performed on Day 9.

He woke within 48 hours with a Glasgow Coma Score of 14, but progressive end-organ dysfunction followed with oliguria and haemofiltration, acute liver injury, gastrointestinal bleeding, hypotension, refractory hypoxia despite ventilation, muscle relaxation and prone ventilation, and refractory metabolic acidosis. The multidisciplinary team judged that ongoing support was not in his best interests, end of life care was instituted and the patient died.
